Nick Woltemade is closing in on a loan move from Newcastle to Juventus, a year after arriving on Tyneside in a club record £69m deal; while Everton are in talks with Monaco over a deal to sign Folarin Balogun after agreeing to sell Beto to Fiorentina.

articles.title: Transfer latest: Juventus in Woltemade loan talks, Everton pushing for Balogun
articles.summary: Palace poised to sign Atalanta defender Ahanor on loan. Forest closing in on Palace’s Muñoz in £22m deal. Nick Woltemade is close to a loan move from Newcastle to Juventus, a year after arriving at Newcastle in a club record £69m deal from Stuttgart.
body: The gifted Germany forward has struggled to impose himself amid the high-intensity gameplans choreographed first by Eddie Howe and now Matthias Jaissle at St James’ Park.

Juventus are one of a handful of clubs – a still interested Borussia Dortmund are among the others – to have inquired about Woltemade’s availability and Newcastle are in negotiations with the Turin club regarding a move involving a loan fee of about £5m.

Any switch for the 24-year-old appears contingent on a forward arriving at St James’ Park, with Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo top of Jaissle’s shopping list and, given the slow pace of negotiations with Lille, Stuttgart’s Morocco international Bilal El Khannouss not far behind.

Woltemade is unlikely to be the only player leaving before Tuesday night’s deadline. The winger Jacob Murphy is wanted by Nottingham Forest, Nick Pope – Jaissle’s third-choice goalkeeper – is looking for a new club and Besiktas retain an interest in Joe Willock.

articles.title: From playing Serena Williams on screen to following in her footsteps
articles.summary: Having played a young Serena Williams on the big screen, teenager Thea Frodin is ready to follow in the American great's footsteps at the US Open.
body: Five years ago, Frodin was chosen as a tennis-playing body double for the actress cast as her childhood idol in the Oscar-nominated film 'King Richard'.
That involved the then 12-year-old working alongside actor Will Smith as he portrayed Richard Williams, the father of sisters Serena and Venus.
"I was honoured. She was one of the players that I looked up to most, just when I was starting to play.
Now, Frodin will make her main-draw singles debut at her home Grand Slam, where Serena and Venus will this year team up in the doubles.

articles.title: Watkins faces Toney clash as strikers push for Saudi supremacy and Tuchel’s attention
articles.summary: Al-Hilal’s signing from Villa is thrown straight into big game against Al-Ahli and faces the highest of expectations. Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney spent 33 minutes on the pitch together a few weeks ago in Miami as England beat France 6-4 in a game for third place at the World Cup.
body: Aston Villa fans will be hoping that, starting against Arsenal on Monday, Nicolas Jackson can quickly help them forget their departed talisman. That’s what Toney did at Brentford back in 2020 when he replaced Watkins. It may not only be supporters in the West Midlands and west London who will be curious to see how their alumni get on in west Asia. England’s heach coach, Thomas Tuchel, will surely tune in (or even turn up?) to get a look at the two forwards battling to become the clear understudy to Harry Kane as a new international cycle starts.

Before that bronze-medal match, Watkins and Toney had enough time together in North America on and off the bench to chat about Saudi Arabia. The former has joined Al-Hilal and probably doesn’t need any advice on how to score goals in the Saudi Pro League but if he does then his Three Lions teammate is the man to ask.

articles.title: Venus Williams bows out after 2am following latest start in US Open history
articles.summary: Kenin wins 6-2, 7-6 (6) in late-night contest. Williams loses 15th straight tour-level match. First-round clash finally begins at 12.13am. Sunday had become Monday by the time Venus Williams finally emerged beneath the closed roof of Arthur Ashe Stadium, her entrance pushed deep into the night…
body: At 46 years old, ranked 611th in the world and making her record-extending 26th US Open singles appearance, Williams has grown accustomed to making history simply by showing up. Even by those standards this latest installment was, as she would later describe it, “completely insane”.

The match itself proved somewhat more straightforward. Williams was beaten 6-2, 7-6 (6) by fellow American wildcard Sofia Kenin in their first-round encounter after 1hr 48min, extending her losing streak at tour level to 15 matches and leaving her without a win at a major tournament since Wimbledon in 2021.

“Venus obviously was playing some amazing tennis,” said Kenin, the 2020 Australian Open champion who also reached the Roland Garros final later that year. “I just tried to keep fighting. I didn’t feel 100% game-wise, some nerves, but I tried to do the best to stay strong in those moments.”

articles.title: Losing Gloucester captaincy was 'brutal' - Ludlow
articles.summary: Gloucester's Lewis Ludlow on losing the captaincy last season, his two England caps, and chasing a record in his upcoming testimonial season.
body: Gloucester flanker Lewis Ludlow says it was "brutal" to lose the club captaincy last August and he would "take it back tomorrow" if offered.
Ludlow has played more than 250 games for the Cherry and Whites and his time as skipper between 2020 and 2025 makes him the longest-serving captain in the club's history.
However, the 31-year-old was replaced by Tomos Williams in the role for the 2025-26 season, although the Welshman signed for Saracens this summer.
"It was brutal," Ludlow told BBC Radio Gloucestershire about being told he was no longer captain.

articles.title: ‘Girls sports are for girls’: Top Democrat agrees with Sophie Cunningham
articles.summary: Last month, Sophie Cunningham ignited a widespread debate throughout the country after she spoke out against transgender women and girls competing in women’s sports. While opinions on the issue are widely split across party lines, with Democrats siding with trans rights and Republicans wanting to…
body: Rob Sand is currently the Democratic nominee in the Iowa gubernatorial race. But while he might be a registered Democrat and the Democratic nominee in the Governor’s race, that doesn’t mean he agrees with Democrats on everything, as he took a stand against trans girls in girls’ sports during a recent interview.

During an interview for the ESPN profile that was published in July, Cunningham was asked a question about her political views when she took the opportunity to share her views on trans women in women’s sports.

“I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that,’” she told ESPN. “I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men.”
Cunningham later doubled down on her comments, saying her opinion was “common sense.”

articles.title: El Chadaille Bitshiabu’s loan to Lens collapses
articles.summary: El Chadaille Bitshiabu’s proposed loan move from RB Leipzig to RC Lens has reportedly collapsed after the two clubs failed to agree the final conditions of the transfer. Leipzig and Lens had been negotiating a season-long loan for the 21-year-old centre-back without a purchase option.
body: The development represents a significant turnaround after negotiations appeared to be at an advanced stage only days ago. Get German Football News previously reported that Leipzig intended to send Bitshiabu to Lens on a developmental loan, with RB continuing to plan around the French defender beyond the coming season. His departure nevertheless appeared increasingly likely heading into the final days of the transfer window. GGFN noted in our latest overview of Leipzig’s remaining transfer business that negotiations with Lens remained unresolved while sporting executive Marcel Schäfer attempted to reduce the size of Martin Demichelis’ squad.

Bitshiabu was omitted from Leipzig’s squad for Saturday’s 3-0 Bundesliga victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach, further underlining the uncertainty surrounding his immediate role. The former Paris Saint-Germain defender’s future is therefore once again open heading into the final stages of the summer window. Leipzig could still attempt to find another temporary destination before the deadline, though Bitshiabu will remain with RB if no alternative solution emerges.

articles.title: Why Arsenal still needed Konsa - despite having so many defenders
articles.summary: The final hours of the transfer window could see Arsenal bring in an attacker. But before the window shuts, a defensive purchase could take centre stage on Monday night.
body: Ezri Konsa could be primed for his Arsenal debut at, of all places, the club he has just departed, Aston Villa. Despite not playing any pre-season football in and around his £51m move to north London, Mikel Arteta says Konsa could be ready for a first Gunners outing at Villa Park.

Konsa is not the signing many expected from Arsenal this summer. Arsenal didn't really need a defender, it's one of their strongest areas of the pitch and the attack needed more attention. But they got him anyway.
That does not make Konsa an unnecessary arrival; this could be the buy that helps shore up Arsenal's title defence.
At 28 years old, Konsa is yet another example of the 'win now' stage of Arteta's Arsenal project. They've got the Premier League title but now the target is to create a dynasty.
